body:
## Problem

In start-command 0.39.0, when a docker task's cgroup counters can't be read from either side, the detached cgroup sampler keeps going for the whole life of the task. That happens when the local cgroup can't be read and `memory.events` doesn't exist inside the container (the `memory` controller isn't delegated). Every interval it starts one `docker exec … sh -c __start_command_cgroup_dir…` and one `docker inspect -f {{.State.Running}}`. None of these rounds can ever produce a sample.

The JSDoc of `buildCgroupSamplerStartSnippet()` (`js/src/lib/cgroup-memory.js`, line 118) says the opposite:

> Without a usable stream it falls back to one `docker exec` per round; without `sh` in the image (exit 126/127) or **without any readable cgroup it records the reason and stops**.

The code only stops on exit 126/127. In the per-round branch a failed read writes `.reason`. Then the liveness check runs, because `__scs_ok` is empty, and the loop sleeps and tries again:

```sh
else __scs_remote=$(docker exec <name> sh -c '…__start_command_cgroup_read /sys/fs/cgroup' 2>&1); __scs_exit=$?;
  if [ "$__scs_exit" = 0 ] && __scs_record "$__scs_remote"; then __scs_ok=1;
  else __scs_detail=…; printf … > "$__start_command_cgroup.reason"; fi; fi;
if [ -z "$__scs_ok" ] && [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' <name> 2>/dev/null)" = false ]; then break; fi;
sleep "$__scs_interval"; done
```

The long-lived stream (#242) exits 3 for unreadable counters, which sets `__scs_stream=0`. So these hosts never use the stream and always land in this per-round branch.

## Measured

This is on a Linux host with cgroup v2, Docker 29.9.1 and the `cgroupfs` driver. The root `cgroup.subtree_control` is `cpuset cpu pids`, so containers have no `memory.events`. The test ran 3 tasks `$ --isolated docker --detached --image alpine:3.20 -- sleep …` for a 60 s window, with a logging `docker` shim first on `PATH`. The script is [`experiments/issue-3614-live-measurement.mjs` in link-assistant/hive-mind#3615](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/3615).

| start-command | `docker` processes per task per minute | monitor shells' CPU per task |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.37.8 | ~97 (`CgroupnsMode` + `exec` + `Running`, ~32 rounds each) | 0.129 cores |
| 0.39.0 | ~22 (`exec` + `Running`, ~11 rounds each) | 0.030–0.037 cores |

0.39.0 is a big improvement (#238). The remaining processes are all failed rounds, though: no sample is ever recorded on this host.

## Expected

Do what the JSDoc says. When the stream ends with "unreadable counters" (exit 3), or the per-round read fails the same way, record the reason and stop sampling. The completion watcher (`docker wait`) still finishes the run. If transient failures need to keep being retried, one option is to stop after N consecutive failed rounds, or to back off exponentially. Either way, a host that can never produce a sample shouldn't pay 2 processes per task every interval.

Found while verifying link-assistant/hive-mind#3614, the issue #238 was filed from.
title: Docker cgroup sampler: with unreadable cgroup counters (no memory controller) the per-round docker exec + docker inspect never stops, despite the JSDoc saying it stops
